hypotheses.mechanism: Most detection-side misses are localisation misses, not missing nuclei. Measured on the lab cache (exp39+ef FN table, all 199 train videos, scratchpad scripts listed in research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_detection.notes.md): the 1,907 a_never FN come from 1,567 distinct GT nodes. For those nodes the nearest raw detector peak (confidence about 1.0) is at a median of 8.65 um: 460 at 7-8 um, 448 at 8-9 um, 235 at 9-10 um. Only about 424 have no peak within 10 um. An image valley test (326 misses, 8 videos) finds an intensity valley between the GT point and the peak in only 4% of cases, so annotation and peak sit on the SAME bright object 7-10 um apart, with the offset mostly along z (|dz| median 4.9 um, 6.5 um in the 7-9 um bin). The same geometry drives swaps: the link-error rate of a matched GT node rises from 2.1% when its nearest peak is within 2 um to 20/25/28% at 4-5/5-6/6-7 um (7,182 such nodes). Per-frame optimal matching then flips the GT track between two predicted tracks. A constant or per-video shift does not help: removing the embryo or video mean offset leaves the share within 7 um at 0.983 against a base of 0.984, and zhincez lost 0.0031 on the LB with a constant shift. Image-moment centroids are worse than the heatmap peak (within 4 um drops from 0.900 to 0.857). So only a LEARNED per-node correction toward where annotators click can pay, which is what the x138 head does. It is limited in three ways: it is trained on 4,136 pairs from 20 movies, it probably takes pairs only inside the 7 um gate so it never sees the 7-10 um tail we lose, it has a 7-point stencil (the centre plus 6 face neighbours on a 1.625 um grid, i.e. about +-1.6 um of context against 5-9 um offsets), and its shift is capped at 2 um, which cannot reach the 9-10 um bin.
hypotheses.change: After the x138 port, retrain the refinement head on our own stack. (1) Capture pass: a Kaggle GPU run in V1284_MODE=capture over all 199 train videos. For every raw peak within 12 um of a GT node, plus a 3% random sample of the other peaks, dump the 32-channel UNet features on a 3x3x3 (optionally 5x5x5) stencil (864-d), the peak_prob, the z index and the xy/z border distances. (2) Pairing: assign the target GT node by track identity, not by nearest neighbour. Use the GT node whose GT track is matched to this peak's final track in the neighbouring frames, which makes pairs out to 10 um trainable. (3) Loss: Huber on the offset plus a gate term, softplus((|p+o-g|-4)/0.5) + 2*softplus((|p+o-g|-7)/0.5), so capacity goes to the 4-7 um swap zone and the 7-10 um tail. (4) Cap at 3 um in z and 2 um in xy. (5) Folds: 5 GroupKFold folds over the 44b6 leak groups and 6bba videos. The final head is trained on all 199 videos. Ship it as a drop-in replacement for the V1284 weights inside the ported patch (same float coordinates and trilinear gather).
hypotheses.upper_bound: Nearest-peak oracle on 133,318 GT nodes. Base: 2,091 nodes at >= 7 um and 7,903 in the 4-7 um zone. Shrinking every offset by 10%/15%/20% gives >=7 um 1,416/1,116/821 and 4-7 um 7,104/6,823/5,735. Value: 1.22 FN per missed node, and one FN->TP is worth about 7.5e-6 (b_break oracle 0.00298/399). Recovering all 1,143 nodes in the 7-10 um tail = 1,390 FN = +0.010, or up to +0.018 if the FP edge to the displaced peak also flips. The swap-zone drop at 20% shrink (-2,168 nodes x (0.24-0.03) error-rate drop ~ 450 involvements) adds about +0.003. Ceiling about +0.013..0.02. For consistency: a 10% shrink predicts +0.006..0.008, which matches x138's single-variable LB step of +0.007.
hypotheses.lab_test: The capture needs about 3-5 GPU h. The rest runs on Kaggle CPU. Step A, OOF geometry on GT nodes. For the ported V1284 head and for the new head, report: share of GT nodes whose nearest refined peak is within 4 um (base 0.925) and within 7 um (base 0.9843), the count at >= 7 um (base 2,091) and the count at 4-7 um (base 7,903), per embryo. Success: >= 7 um <= 0.80x of what the public head reaches, on both embryos. Step B, exact lab replay: shift the final exp48(+ef) node coordinates by the OOF offsets (peak nodes directly; synthetic gap nodes get the interpolation of their neighbours' offsets), write float coordinates and score with the official scorer. This lower-bounds the gain because the edge transformer is not re-run. Gate: SELECTION -> one CONFIRMATION run, >= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, >= 55% of videos gaining. Then one LB probe: exp48+port+newhead against exp48+port.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.002..+0.005 public over the port. Arithmetic: if the retrained head moves the effective shrink from about 10% (public head, -10.4% centre error held out) to 13-16%, the 7-10 um tail drops by another 300-450 nodes, i.e. 370-550 FN x 7.5e-6 = +0.003..0.004, plus the swap zone +0.0005..0.001. It could reach +0.006 if the 3 um cap and the track-identity pairs unlock the 9-10 um bin (235 nodes).
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium. The public detector was trained on all 199 videos, so peaks on train are in-sample and closer to GT than on test, and the head learns an under-sized correction. That errs in the safe direction, and x138 was trained the same way and still gained +0.007. The annotation convention differs by embryo (6bba mean dz -0.85 um, 44b6 -0.17 um, per-video q10/q90 -1.34/+0.16), so an embryo-fold readout (train on 6bba, test on 44b6 and the reverse) is mandatory. A wider cap raises the risk of moving correct nodes out of the gate, so gate on both 'crossed in' and 'crossed out' counts.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Detector fine-tunes, weight soups and TTA variants change the UNet or the views. This keeps the detector frozen and learns only a coordinate head on its features. The brief excludes only the port itself; this is a retrain with a new objective, a new pairing and new inputs, motivated by the measured 7-10 um tail that the public head cannot reach with its cap and stencil. The constant shift (zhincez) is a different, falsified mechanism: we show per-video mean removal gives 0.9835 vs 0.9843.

hypotheses.mechanism: The localisation error is partly persistent along a track and partly frame noise. Along GT single-child chains (about 120k pairs), the autocorrelation of the peak-minus-GT offset is 0.57 (z) / 0.49 (y) / 0.47 (x) at lag 1 and falls to 0.31/0.19/0.20 at lag 5. The dz sign of a missed node agrees with its GT predecessor's offset in 82% of cases (n=825). The whole track hovers: the missed nodes' predecessors have a nearest-peak distance of median 7.8 um. So about half of the offset variance is frame-level, and a per-node head sees one frame of noisy evidence. Pooling head outputs along the linked track averages out the head's own noise and keeps the persistent component. The pipeline already shows this: linefit smoothing of positions is its largest post-processing stage (+0.0145). In our measurement, nodes that linefit pulls INTO the 7 um gate have larger displacements (median 1.6 um, q75 2.2 um) than those it pushes out (median 1.3 um), and a 2 um displacement cap would lose 75 crossings in to save 15 crossings out. Smoothing therefore works at the gate, but today it smooths quantised peak positions, not the learned offsets.
hypotheses.change: Add a post-link stage after linefit, before writing: for each node on a single-parent/single-child chain (forks and DaughterNet-inserted daughters are skipped), compute its final offset as o_i' = w*o_i + (1-w)*median(o_j over linked nodes j within +-k frames). Here o is the refinement-head offset (the port's V1284 head, or hypothesis 1's head). Grid: k in {1,2,3}, w in {0.3,0.5,0.7}. Variant B: apply the head to the linefit-smoothed position instead of the raw peak (order swap). Variant C: a small second-stage MLP that takes [o_{t-1}, o_t, o_{t+1}, the three peak_probs, |step|] and predicts the residual, trained OOF on the same capture. It is deterministic, CPU-only, about 30 lines in the tail and shippable in the kernel.
hypotheses.upper_bound: After a head the residual lost tail is about 1,100-1,400 nodes (10-15% shrink oracle). If about 50% of the residual offset variance is frame-level and pooling over 5 frames removes about 80% of that part, the residual lost count can fall by about 25-35% in the best case: 300-450 nodes x 1.22 FN x 7.5e-6 = +0.003..0.004 (+0.006 if the displaced FP edges flip). GT annotation noise is also frame-independent, and pooling cannot fix it, so the true ceiling is lower.
hypotheses.lab_test: Uses the capture from hypothesis 1, or only the port's head outputs on captured features, all on CPU. Compare the OOF geometry (counts at >= 7 um and at 4-7 um, per embryo) for per-node head versus pooled variants, then run the exact lab replay of the shifted final graph (official scorer) with SELECTION -> CONFIRMATION. Success: >= +0.001 over the per-node head on CONFIRMATION with each embryo >= +0.0005, so that bundled with the head it passes the +0.002 gate. Check that pooling never increases the 'crossed out of 7 um' count by more than 20% of 'crossed in'.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.0005..+0.002 on top of the head. Pooling mostly helps the 4-7 um swap zone (error rate 20-28%) and the 7-8 um bin (460 nodes). About 150-250 recovered nodes gives +0.001..0.002.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low to medium. It uses only our own graph and head outputs, with no train-video GT at inference. It fails if linking errors (swaps) contaminate the pooling window. To mitigate, pool only over chains whose edge_prob >= 0.7 and never across forks. It depends on hypothesis 1 or the port being in place.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Linefit weight and window were swept and closed (B28), but on quantised peak positions. This pools the learned refinement offsets, a new signal that did not exist before the port. Our measurement shows the only linefit alternative with a mechanism (a displacement cap) is negative, so this is the other direction: more temporal pooling on better inputs. It is not a relink or association knob; edges are untouched.

hypotheses.mechanism: The 3 um NMS runs on a 1.625 um isotropic heatmap grid, which lets through duplicate peaks of ONE nucleus at 2-3 grid steps. There are 46,169 same-frame raw pairs under 5 um (histogram spikes at 3.25/3.63/3.98/4.6/4.875 um), and an image valley test on 300 sampled pairs finds a valley (two objects) in only 3%. In the final exp39 graph, 63,253 nodes (1.53%) still have a same-frame neighbour under 5 um. Evaluable edges touching them are FP at 35.9% (<4 um) and 19.6% (4-5 um), against 1.4% for isolated nodes: 450 of the 6,846 FP. GT nodes with a second peak under 4/5 um are in link errors 44%/26% of the time. This is the forum's 'duplicates steal links'. Blind collapse is harmful, though. For the 1,440 GT nodes with such a pair, the share within 4 um falls from 0.947 (nearest member) to 0.776 with the midpoint and to 0.635 when the higher-peak_prob member is kept. The heavier NMS was -0.026. So the choice of survivor must be learned or trajectory-based. A head-free trajectory rule (keep the member closest to the previous-frame peak) picks the GT-nearest member 88% of the time (<4 um 0.890).
hypotheses.change: A graph-level step after the ILP/relink and before the tail. For same-frame node pairs under 5 um with no intensity valley on the TTA-averaged heatmap/image profile (min along the segment >= 0.85 x the smaller end), collapse the pair only if their REFINED positions (port head, or hypothesis 1's head) are within 2.5 um of each other. The survivor is the member whose refined position lies nearer the track's linefit prediction from t-1/t+1. The union of in/out edges is re-resolved by edge_prob, keeping at most 1 in and 2 out. The fallback without a head is the trajectory rule alone. Forks from safe divisions and DaughterNet are never touched.
hypotheses.upper_bound: FP edges on <5 um pairs: 450. FN involvement of GT nodes with d2 < 5 um: about 500 nodes. Fixing all of them gives (450 + ~400 FN edges) x 7.5e-6 ~ +0.0064. The node term: collapsing about 30k nodes (0.75% of 4.13M) is worth +0.0007 (1% fewer nodes = +0.00092). Ceiling about +0.007.
hypotheses.lab_test: Run the trajectory-rule variant today in the exact lab replay (CPU, Kaggle lab kernel): SELECTION grid over the radius {4.0, 4.5, 5.0} um, the valley on/off and the survivor rule {trajectory, max-prob}, then one CONFIRMATION run. Readout: FP on edges touching the collapsed pairs (target -30%), TP loss <= 0.3 x FP removed, node ratio, and score gated at >= +0.002 with each embryo >= +0.001. After the capture exists, rerun with the head-refined survivor choice. The image valley needs the zarr frames, which the Kaggle lab kernel has.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.0005..+0.002. Roughly a third of the 450 FP and a quarter of the ~500 swap-zone involvements fixed (~250 edges x 7.5e-6 = +0.0019) minus 3-6% localisation losses on annotated duplicates (about 60 nodes, -0.0007), plus the node term +0.0004..0.0007.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium. Duplicate frequency depends on the detector's calibration on the hidden embryos; a denser or dimmer embryo may have more real neighbours under 5 um. The valley gate and the refined-position agreement are the guards. The public-LB node-multiplier artefact (min-track-length) does not apply because tracks stay continuous.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: B31 clustering was closed at step 1 because radii of 0.5-2 um cannot merge anything under a 3 um NMS; it never tried 3-5 um with edge union. The heavier NMS kernel ((5,5,5), -0.026) deletes peaks before linking without choosing the right survivor and also kills real 5-5.6 um neighbours. B25 pruning removed nodes inside tracks without re-attaching edges. This rule is valley-gated, re-attaches edges, and picks the survivor by trajectory or learned refinement, which our data shows is decisive (0.635 with max-prob vs 0.890 with trajectory vs 0.947 oracle).

hypotheses.mechanism: The UNet heatmap and features live on a 1.625 um isotropic grid (xy is downsampled 4x), so raw peak coordinates are quantised at 1.625 um on every axis (RMS about 0.8 um in 3D). The V1284 head only sees the 32-channel features at the peak and its 6 face neighbours on that coarse grid. The image itself is 0.406 um in xy. Naive image moments are worse than the heatmap peak (within 4 um 0.900 -> 0.857, within 7 um 0.979 -> 0.966 on 611 GT nodes), so the extra resolution only pays through a LEARNED model of the annotators' convention. In addition, the public UNet was trained on all 199 train videos, so any head on its features has an in-sample readout. A small CNN trained from scratch on full-resolution raw patches with folds by leak group gives an honest OOF estimate of refinement gain for the first time. It is also a model with independent errors that can be stacked on the V1284 offsets, which lowers the variance on unseen embryos.
hypotheses.change: Train a small 3D CNN (4 conv blocks, about 200k parameters) on raw image patches of 9x33x33 voxels (14.6 x 13.4 x 13.4 um), normalised per patch (median/IQR). The patches are centred at the V1284-refined peak and sampled at t-1, t and t+1 (3 channels) plus a channel with a Gaussian marker. Targets are the residual offsets to the GT node, from track-identity pairs up to 10 um (about 130k pairs), with a Gaussian NLL loss (mean + log-variance). Use 5 folds by leak group on Kaggle T4, about 30-60 min. At inference (inside the kernel, on the images already in memory), apply shift = clip(mu, 3 um z / 2 um xy) only where predicted sigma < s0 (s0 tuned on OOF). Otherwise keep the V1284 position. Zero-training ablation in the same capture: a quadratic sub-grid fit of the TTA-averaged logits over the 3x3x3 neighbourhood, used as the input position.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Same oracle as hypothesis 1. Full removal of the grid quantisation alone is about 0.66 um^2 of variance, which is roughly 10% of d for typical nodes but under 1% for the 7-9 um tail. So the real ceiling comes from learning the convention: up to a 20% shrink, i.e. >= 7 um 2,091 -> 821 and a combined score ceiling of about +0.013..0.02, shared with hypothesis 1 (the two are not additive beyond the oracle).
hypotheses.lab_test: Patch extraction needs only the zarr frames and the lab cache, so it runs as a Kaggle CPU kernel plus a T4 fold training, and needs NO UNet capture for the standalone variant, which can start before the port lands. Readout: OOF share within 4 um and 7 um and the >= 7 um count per embryo against the raw peaks (0.925 / 0.9843 / 2,091). Success standalone: >= 7 um count reduced by >= 20% on both embryos with 'crossed out' < 25% of 'crossed in'. Stacked: a further >= 10% on top of the V1284 head. Then the exact lab replay of the shifted final graph under the SELECTION/CONFIRMATION gate (>= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001).
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.001..+0.004 on top of the ported head, if stacking reduces the residual lost tail by 150-450 nodes (x 1.22 FN x 7.5e-6). Standalone without the port it could be worth up to about +0.005, which makes it a hedge if the V1284 weights transfer poorly.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium. Intensity statistics of the hidden embryos differ (per-patch normalisation helps). The convention learned on train (6bba-heavy: 1,890 of the 2,091 lost nodes) may not hold on test, so embryo-fold readouts (6bba->44b6 and the reverse) must both be positive. The inference cost is small (about 20k patches per video through a tiny CNN).
hypotheses.not_closed_because: It is not a detector fine-tune, a soup or a TTA variant: the UNet and its outputs stay unchanged. It is a separate coordinate model on raw pixels. It is not the port: it uses different inputs (full-resolution image, 3 frames) and is trained fold-clean on our 199 videos. The image-moment centroid we tested is negative, which is exactly why the proposal is a learned residual model rather than a geometric rule.
